title: Arutmin Borneo Run 2026 Review: What the 2025 Race Was Like
seo_title: Arutmin Borneo Run Review: Banjarbaru Course, Cut-offs, Sell-out
meta_description: Arutmin Borneo Run review from the 2025 race: the undulating Banjarbaru loop, 25°C and 94% humidity at the start, a four-hour half limit and a five-minute sell-out.
dek: What it was like to run South Kalimantan's biggest road race in November 2025: the loop through Banjarbaru, the humid pre-dawn air, the aid stations and cut-offs, and how hard it is to get a place.
verdict: Enter if you want a certified, well-supported half marathon in Kalimantan and can be online the moment entries open. The 2025 race drew 4,050 runners to an undulating loop through Banjarbaru with 104 m of climbing, nine water stations and a generous four-hour limit. At the 5.30am reading it was already 25°C with 94% humidity and a thunderstorm nearby, and 27°C by 9am. The catches are access and air: the first 3,000 places went in five minutes, and prize money is for Indonesians only. Be online the moment entries open.

sections.heading: The Course: An Undulating Loop Through Banjarbaru
paragraphs: The race starts and finishes at the South Kalimantan governor's office complex in Banjarbaru [1]. On the half-marathon map posted on the race website, the first 6 km wind around the roundabouts of the government complex, with two U-turns. The route then heads out along Jalan Aneka Tambang and Jalan H. Mistar Cokrokusumo, runs west along Jalan Trikora past the Al-Munawwarah grand mosque to the Trikora roundabout at km 15, and comes back along Jalan Palam Raya and Jalan Banua Praja Barat to the finish [2].

It is not flat. The map puts the start at 48 m, the high point at 59 m and the total climb at 104 m, with the highest ground around the middle of the race and the lowest a few kilometres from the end; the PASI measurement certificate describes the road as undulating [2][3]. PASI, Indonesia's athletics federation, measured the course in October 2023, and the certificate is valid until 5 November 2026, but any change to the course, however small, voids it [3]. The map is the one posted for 2026; no separate 2025 map could be found.

sections.heading: The Weather: Saturated Air and a Storm Nearby
paragraphs: Syamsudin Noor airport, in Banjarbaru about 8 km west of the start, recorded 25°C at 5am on race morning with a dew point of 25°C and 100% humidity [4]. At 5.30am it was 25°C with 94% humidity, a 5-knot wind and a thunderstorm reported in the vicinity [4]. The air stayed at 24°C to 25°C until 7.30am, then warmed to 26°C at 8am, 27°C at 9am and 29°C at 9.30am, around the time the half marathon closed [4].

A dew point of 24°C to 25°C means sweat barely evaporates, so pace for the air rather than the distance. From a 5.20am start, a two-hour half marathoner was finished by about 7.20am in 24°C to 25°C air; a runner near the four-hour limit spent the last hour at 26°C to 29°C.

sections.heading: Aid Stations and Cut-offs
paragraphs: The half-marathon map marks nine water stations, the first near km 2 and the last near km 17, plus sponge points near km 9 and km 14, water-dousing points near km 12 and km 16, and sprinklers on the run-in [2]. The LariKu race listing gave the same nine water stations for the half in 2025, with four on the 10 km and two on the 5 km [5]. After the finish there is water, an isotonic drink and bananas [6].

The limits are generous: four hours for the half, two for the 10 km and 90 minutes for the 5 km in 2025 [5], and the same for 2026, when the half also has one checkpoint at km 15 after 2 hours 45 minutes [7]. That checkpoint works out to 11 minutes per km. The listing gave 2025 start times of 5.20am for the half, 5.45am for the 10 km and 6am for the 5 km [5]; for 2026 the half starts at 5.15am [7]. Runners up to 10 minutes late may still start; later than that, they go off with the next race [7].
For 2026 the rules add a team of running doctors who run in every category [7].

sections.heading: Getting a Place
paragraphs: This is the hard part. For the 2025 race the first 3,000 places sold out in five minutes, and a second batch of 1,050 went in three [8]. The organiser said it had planned for 3,000 runners and expanded to 4,050 because of demand [9]. Runners came from across Kalimantan and from Java, Sumatra, Sulawesi and Papua [8].
For 2026 the organiser has raised the field to 6,500 places, more than 50% up on 2025 [10].

sections.heading: Race Weekend and the Rules
paragraphs: Race packs in 2025 were collected on 21 and 22 November at the Novotel ballroom in Banjarbaru [5]; for 2026 the dates are 30 and 31 October, with the venue to be confirmed [7]. The 2025 listing gave entry fees of Rp450,000 for the half, Rp350,000 for the 10 km and Rp150,000 or Rp200,000 for the 5 km; every finisher got a medal, and half-marathon finishers a finisher tee [5]. Baggage drop opens at 4am, and suitcases are not accepted [6].

Entries cannot be refunded or transferred [6]. Cash prizes go to the top five in each class and only to Indonesian citizens [7], and total prize money in 2025 was Rp385 million [8]. The FAQ says foreigners may enter [6], but the rules page describes the race as open to Indonesian citizens with Indonesian ID [7].

The race is managed by IdeaRun, which shares a 12-week training plan for beginners on social media and includes disabled and older people as runners and staff [1]. The 2025 race was streamed live on IdeaRun's YouTube channel [8].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2026 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a certified half marathon in Kalimantan with a generous limit and good aid, and you can be ready the moment entries open. The 10 km and 5 km suit newer runners, and many 2025 entrants were trying longer distances for the first time [9].

Think twice if you want a flat course or a fast time: the loop climbs 104 m in total [2]. If you are coming from abroad, prize money is for Indonesians only and the official pages disagree on whether foreigners may enter [7][6], so ask the organiser before you pay.
The 2026 race is on Sunday 1 November, with the half starting at 5.15am [7].

Nobody from this site ran the race. This review draws on the organiser's race information, route map and course certificate, a race listing, airport weather records and local news reports in Indonesian.

faqs.question: How fast does the Arutmin Borneo Run sell out?
faqs.answer: Within minutes. For the 2025 race the first 3,000 places went in five minutes and a second batch of 1,050 went in three. The organiser has raised the 2026 field to 6,500 places, more than 50% up, but on 2025's evidence you should be online the moment registration opens.

faqs.question: What are the cut-off times at the Arutmin Borneo Run?
faqs.answer: Generous. The half marathon allows four hours from the gun, with one checkpoint at km 15 after 2 hours 45 minutes. The 10 km allows two hours and the 5 km 90 minutes. For 2026 the half starts at 5.15am, the 10 km at 5.45am and the 5 km at 6am, local time.

faqs.question: Is the Arutmin Borneo Run course hilly?
faqs.answer: Gently. The official half-marathon map shows a start at 48 m, a high point of 59 m and 104 m of climbing in total, and the PASI certificate describes the road as undulating. The loop runs from the governor's office complex through Banjarbaru along Jalan Trikora and back, and was measured by PASI in 2023.

faqs.question: How hot and humid is the Arutmin Borneo Run?
faqs.answer: Warm and very humid. At 5.30am on race morning in 2025, Banjarbaru's airport recorded 25°C, 94% humidity and a thunderstorm nearby, with a dew point of 24°C to 25°C all morning. It stayed at 24°C to 25°C until 7.30am, then reached 27°C by 9am and 29°C by 9.30am.

faqs.question: Can foreigners run the Arutmin Borneo Run?
faqs.answer: Possibly, but check first. The 2026 FAQ says foreign runners are welcome but cannot win prizes, which go only to Indonesian citizens, while the rules page describes the race as open to Indonesian citizens with Indonesian ID. Entries cannot be refunded or transferred, so confirm with the organiser before paying.

editorial_notes: Rewritten 2026-09-28 about the previous edition (Sunday 23 November 2025). Weather is from Syamsudin Noor airport METAR observations, not a forecast. The official site now shows only 2026 information; 2025 start times, cut-offs, fees and water-station counts come from the LariKu race listing (the 2025 half start is 5.20am there; an earlier official page, not readable, may have said 5.30am). The route map and PASI certificate are the ones posted for 2026; the certificate dates from 2023 and lapses on any course change, so the map is taken as the 2025 loop, and the review says this is an inference. The 5 km field is 850 in the post-race report and 740 in the chair's press-conference figure; 850 is used. The official FAQ and rules disagree on whether foreigners may enter; both are given. Results were behind a bot check and no winners' times appeared in readable reports, so the review has no field-speed section. No rating. ANTARA's reports are not cited: its terms forbid use of its pages for AI; facts only ANTARA reported (the field split by distance, the finish-line snack, the gun start, disabled runners, and September 2026 haze) are left out.
